passages.title: Task 7 – short texts
paragraphs: 7.1 Sarah’s Blog: Last month Sarah took part in a school cooking competition. She sent in a toasted-sandwich recipe seen on TV, made it in the school cafeteria and met celebrity chef Tom Burns, who praised her sandwich. She did not reach the top three. Options: A won first prize; B met a famous person; C made a snack from her family cookbook.

7.2 Advertisement: Choose a personalised present such as a flash drive, power bank, mug, bag or calendar, and add your own photo or text. Options: A learn how to make a gadget; B find a birthday-party venue; C give someone a special gift.

7.3 Mum’s note: Jim should take Amy to her friend’s birthday party at the Kids’ Club on his way to football practice. Taxi money is on the kitchen table. Options: A give Jim instructions; B encourage Jim to go to training; C thank Jim for his help.

7.4 Holly’s World: Holly’s grandma’s café is losing customers to a new shopping centre, so Holly organises a singing competition in the café. Options: A Holly’s idea to make the café popular again; B an event at the shopping centre; C Holly’s work as a waitress.

passages.title: Discovery in a chimney
paragraphs: While renovating a house in Surrey, a builder found an old envelope in an unused chimney. It contained a 70-year-old letter in which seven-year-old Tom asked Santa for coloured pencils and a woollen hat.
The builder posted a photo online to show how much times had changed. Tom, now an old man, recognised the letter and contacted him. The builder gave him a large box of pencils and a woollen hat.
Tom decided to give the pencils to a boy from a poor family and keep the hat as a reminder that dreams can come true.

passages.title: Museum ships
paragraphs: A. The Mary Rose, Henry VIII’s flagship, sank in 1545 and was raised from the sea in 1982. It and the objects found inside can be seen in a Portsmouth museum.
B. The Cutty Sark opened to visitors in 1954. On board, people dressed as historical characters tell stories about the crew’s everyday life.
C. Francis Drake sailed around the world on the Pelican, later renamed the Golden Hinde. The original was destroyed; a copy built in 1973 lets visitors experience a sailor’s life.
passages.source: Na podstawie: maryrose.org, rmg.co.uk i goldenhinde.co.uk.

passages.title: The Railway Children
paragraphs: A theatre adaptation of Edith Nesbit’s novel is performed on a stage in an unused part of a real railway station. Bobbie, Peter and Phyllis move to the countryside after their father suddenly disappears. A real steam train appears in the last scene.
Mike writes that the tickets were expensive but worthwhile. After the play he could enter the steam train and then visited a station bookshop offering books at half price.

passages.title: A furry champion
paragraphs: Paris is a twelve-year-old Beagle with a talent for catching footballs. Last year she broke the Guinness World Record for the largest number caught by a dog in one minute. She practises for fifteen minutes every afternoon. Her owner asks readers to let them know if their dogs can do similar tricks.

passages.title: Quilling – art for everyone
paragraphs: Quilling is a way of creating pictures from coloured paper strips. You use scissors, glue and metal tools to hold the strips and give them the shapes you want. It may be difficult at first, but practice helps.
passages.source: Na podstawie: quillingcards.net, loveart.pl i amazon.in.
